lines: Not on this street. Not one note.
In Hamelin, Germany, there is one street where nobody plays music. Not for five hundred years. Because of what happened here, in twelve eighty-four.
The town was full of rats. In the bread. In the beds.
Then a stranger came, in a coat of many colours.
Every rat. Gone. For a thousand coins.
He played one tune, and every rat in Hamelin followed him... straight into the river.
asking a question with rising pitch, hopeful, curious
The rats are gone! Why would we pay?
The piper didn't argue. He just left.
A man like that doesn't argue... He comes back.
On the twenty-sixth of June, while the grown-ups sat in church, he came back. With a new tune.
One by one, the children opened their doors and followed him. Down this street. Out of the gate. Up the hill... into the fog.
A hundred and thirty children. And the fog closed behind them.
Only a few stayed. One too slow to keep up. One who couldn't hear the song.
The town wrote it down. It is a hundred years since our children left. And on this street... nobody plays music. Still.
Now. The five euros you promised me.
